title: The Earth Weeps Before Brahma
story:
The earth had grown too heavy to bear. It was not the weight of mountains or rivers or the countless creatures that walk upon her back; that weight she had always carried gladly, the way a mother carries a sleeping child. What pressed upon her now was the weight of kings.

These were not kings at all, though they wore crowns and commanded armies. They were demons who had taken birth in royal houses, taking the name and the power of rulers and using both for nothing but to crush whatever lay beneath them. Where a true king should guard his people the way a father guards his children, these lords trampled them instead. And there were so many of them, hundreds of thousands spread across the land, that the earth herself felt the weight of every footstep, every marching army, every unjust command.

For the earth is not mere soil. In the oldest telling she is a living being, patient beyond measure, who feeds every creature from her body and asks nothing in return. But even her patience has an end, and under that burden she grew exhausted. The strength that kept her fields level and her rivers in their courses began to fail, and the life she sheltered grew dim. She who had always given began, at last, to falter under what was taken.

So she did the one thing left to a creature who has borne too much. She took the form of a cow.

It was not a gesture of fear but of speech. The cow is the gentlest of creatures, the one that gives milk and asks only for grass, and to appear in that shape before the creator was to say, without a word, that the world had been reduced to something helpless, a thing to be driven and milked and forgotten. She who gave her milk to all now came asking only to be left with enough strength to go on giving. And she wept. The tears ran down her face as she stood before Brahma, the maker of the worlds, worn and trembling, and poured out her long misery.

She did not ask for a champion to fight her battles, or for a new king to rule her. She asked only to be unburdened, to be relieved of the weight that was slowly crushing the life out of her. It was a small thing to ask, and an enormous one: a whole world, bent and weeping, laying its trouble at the feet of its maker.

Brahma heard her, and he understood what the tears meant: the world he had made was being unmade by those who should have guarded it. The plea did not vanish into silence. It would be heard.
reflection: The earth's suffering is given a body so that it can be heard: she sends no messenger and offers no prayer, but comes herself, in the gentlest of forms, and lets her tears speak for a whole world.
next_story_tease: But her tears alone could not lift the burden; the plea would have to travel farther still.
hero_scene: The earth, in the form of a weary, weeping cow, standing before Brahma as tears fall down her face, pleading to be relieved of the crushing weight of countless demon kings.
visual_elements: Earth in the form of a gentle cow
the invisible weight of demon kings
a mood of sorrow and appeal
